My land here in Quzhou is about 6 mu. My father farmed it the same way, and his father before him. I know this soil. I know what it wants.

I will grow winter wheat and summer maize, same as always. That is what everyone here grows. The wheat goes in the ground in October after the maize comes off, and the maize goes back in June after the wheat is cut. Two crops, same field, every year. I don't have time or money to try something different and risk a bad harvest.

For wheat seeds, I buy the improved variety from the township supply cooperative — Jimai seeds, the ones most people around here use. I have tried saving my own seed before but the yields dropped, so now I buy new seed each year. For maize I always buy hybrid seed. Everyone does now. The hybrid gives much better ears.

Fertilizer — I apply a bag of compound fertilizer at planting and then spread urea when the plants are growing. Maybe I use a bit more than I need to, but I would rather the crop not go hungry. I learned the amounts from watching my neighbors and from doing this for 40 years.

I plough the wheat field in autumn to break the hard crust after maize. For maize in summer I just do rotary tillage — faster, and the soil is softer then anyway.

Irrigation: wheat needs water at jointing and heading for sure, and I'll add one more at sowing if autumn is dry. Maize gets summer rain mostly, but I'll pump once if it's dry during pollination.

Pesticides: wheat gets sprayed twice — once for aphids in spring, once for fungal disease before heading. Maize I watch and usually spray once for corn borer.
